<div class="proj-layout">
<div class="proj-main">
<div class="proj-glance">
<p class="glance-role"><i class="bi bi-person-check" aria-hidden="true"></i>First author (AMM, SEGRE)</p>
<ul class="glance-tags" aria-label="Scale and methods"><li>Multi-tier supply chain</li><li>On-site wind, solar, storage</li><li>Hourly grid buying and selling</li><li>52 weeks of 168 hours</li><li>Mixed-integer location model</li></ul>
</div>
<section class="proj-q" aria-labelledby="h-question">
<h2 id="h-question"><i class="bi bi-question-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>Research question</h2>
<p class="proj-question">Where should a manufacturing supply chain place its facilities, and how much on-site wind, solar and storage should each facility install when facilities can trade energy with the grid?</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-insight" id="insight" aria-labelledby="h-insight">
<h2 id="h-insight"><i class="bi bi-stars" aria-hidden="true"></i>Key insight</h2>
<p class="insight-title">With on-site renewables, wind and sun become part of the siting decision</p>
<p>When each facility can install its own wind, solar and storage and trade energy with the grid, a candidate site&#x27;s renewable resource affects its operating cost. The model then weighs transport cost against resource quality, and storage became worthwhile under high peak prices or capped grid imports.</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" aria-labelledby="h-contribution">
<h2 id="h-contribution"><i class="bi bi-person-check" aria-hidden="true"></i>My contribution</h2>
<p>First author of the location-allocation papers (AMM, SEGRE), for which I did most of the work. Second author of the JORS paper, for which I contributed to the optimization models and the case-study analyses.</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" id="approach" aria-labelledby="h-approach">
<h2 id="h-approach"><i class="bi bi-tools" aria-hidden="true"></i>How I approached it</h2>
<ol class="approach">
<li class="ap-card"><p class="ap-challenge"><span class="ap-k">Challenge</span>Where a facility opens decides its wind and solar resource, while transport, production and energy costs depend on the same decisions.</p><p class="ap-did"><span class="ap-k">What I did</span>With my co-authors, I developed a mixed-integer model that opens factories and warehouses, routes products and sizes each open site&#x27;s wind, solar and storage, with an hourly energy balance and grid trade.</p><p class="ap-why"><span class="ap-k">Why it mattered</span>Solving these together showed that facility siting trades transport cost against renewable resource quality.</p></li>
<li class="ap-card"><p class="ap-challenge"><span class="ap-k">Challenge</span>Weekly store demand is uncertain, yet the network has to meet it reliably.</p><p class="ap-did"><span class="ap-k">What I did</span>I modeled demand as a chance constraint with a set service level, written as its deterministic equivalent.</p><p class="ap-why"><span class="ap-k">Why it mattered</span>The model stays a mixed-integer linear program while holding the chance of a stock-out to the chosen level.</p></li>
</ol>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" aria-labelledby="h-method">
<h2 id="h-method"><i class="bi bi-diagram-3" aria-hidden="true"></i>Method</h2>
<p>JORS sizes on-site microgrids for fixed facility locations with production and inventory planning; AMM and SEGRE add facility location-allocation decisions.</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" aria-labelledby="h-findings">
<h2 id="h-findings"><i class="bi bi-lightbulb" aria-hidden="true"></i>Key findings</h2>
<ol class="findings">
<li>Facility siting trades transport cost against renewable resource quality (AMM).</li>
<li>On-site renewables lower total supply-chain cost under the modeled time-of-use tariffs.</li>
<li>In the AMM price scenarios, batteries became attractive at high peak electricity prices; in JORS, capping grid imports made storage worthwhile.</li>
</ol>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec proj-bounds" aria-labelledby="h-bounds">
<h2 id="h-bounds"><i class="bi bi-exclamation-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>Boundary conditions</h2>
<p>Stylized multi-echelon networks with synthetic distances and costs.</p>
</section>
